title: A sharp fs monoid is the lattice part of its rational cone
statement: Let $P$ be a finitely generated integral saturated commutative monoid, written additively [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], and assume $P$ is sharp: $0$ is its only invertible element. Let $G=P^{\rm gp}$, put $V=G\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$, and let $C\subseteq V$ be the rational cone generated by the image of $P$, namely the set of finite sums $\sum_i q_i(p_i\otimes1)$ with $q_i\in\mathbf Q_{\ge0}$ and $p_i\in P$. Then: (a) $G$ is a free abelian group of finite rank, that is, it has a finite $\mathbf Z$-basis, so that $g\mapsto g\otimes1$ embeds $G$ in $V$; (b) $C$ is a pointed rational polyhedral cone spanning $V$, meaning that there are finitely many $v_1,\ldots,v_m\in G$ with $C=\{\sum_j q_jv_j:q_j\in\mathbf Q_{\ge0}\}$, that $C\cap(-C)=\{0\}$, and that every element of $V$ is a difference of two elements of $C$; (c) $P=C\cap G$ inside $V$. The case $P=\{0\}$, $G=0$, $V=0$, $C=\{0\}$ is included.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.1.17, printed p. 101 (saturation), and Remark 3.1.29, printed p. 103 (rational polyhedral fan description); the lattice-cone formulation is expanded here. Kato 1994, Toric singularities, is WANTED for the underlying toric monoid argument.
